title: Why Saturn Might Lose Its Rings Within Your Lifetime
hook: Saturn's rings are a ticking clock, and the planet is eating them alive.
closing: So catch Saturn's rings now -- grain by grain, they're already running out.
question: Will Saturn's rings outlive us?

segments.say: Saturn's rings are raining down into the planet right now. They'll be gone in under 300 million years.
Saturn is about 4,500 million years old. Its rings are nearly out of time, a blink by comparison.
Icy ring material falls into Saturn's atmosphere fast enough to fill a swimming pool every half hour. Scientists call it ring rain.
